declarations.description:
A collapsible, searchable JSON tree. Every line can copy its path or its value.

Hand it any JSON value through `data`, as a property or as a JSON string in the attribute:

```html
<c2-json-viewer data='{"user":{"name":"Ada","roles":["admin"]}}'></c2-json-viewer>
```

The top-level entries of an object or array are the first lines; a branch shows its size while collapsed.
`expand-depth` decides how many levels start open, and `expandAll()` / `collapseAll()` reset every branch.
A branch with more than `page-size` children shows that many and a "show more" line for the rest.

`search` highlights every key and value containing the text (case-insensitive) and opens the branches on the
way to each match; `filter` also hides the lines that lead to no match. The viewer has no search box of its
own, so pair it with `c2-search-field`. `searchMatches` lists the paths that matched.

Only the lines in view are rendered, so a document with hundreds of thousands of visible lines scrolls like a short
one; each line is one row high and a long value is cut off with an ellipsis (its full text is in the tooltip and in
"copy value"). Treat `data` as immutable: assign a new value rather than mutating the current one, since the viewer
caches each object's keys.

Paths are written as JSONPath (`$.user.roles[0]`) or, with `path-format="pointer"`, as JSON Pointer
(`/user/roles/0`). A circular reference shows as `[Circular]` rather than recursing.

### Keyboard

Arrow Up and Down walk the lines. Arrow Right opens a branch, then moves to its first child; Arrow Left closes
it, then moves to its parent. Page Up and Page Down move a screen at a time, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space toggle a branch (or reveal the
rest of a long one), `*` opens every sibling. `C` (or Ctrl/Cmd + C) copies the focused line's value, `P` its path.

members.description: Paths of the nodes matching `search`, in document order, written in `path-format`.

members.name: pageStep
members.description: `page-size` as a positive whole number, so a zero, negative or fractional value still pages forward.

members.name: expandAll
members.description: Opens every branch.

members.name: collapseAll
members.description: Closes every branch, leaving the top-level entries.

members.name: boxHeight
members.description: Height of the line box: every line, until that outgrows SCROLL_HEIGHT_LIMIT.

members.name: lineAt
members.description:
Which line (fractional) sits at scroll offset `y`. The scroll range maps onto the line range, so the top shows the
first line and the bottom the last; without compression this is simply `y / rowHeight`.

members.name: offsetOf
members.description: The inverse of lineAt: the scroll offset at which `line` is the first one shown.

members.name: updateWindow
members.description: Works out which lines intersect both the viewport and the viewer's own scroll box.

members.name: renderKey
members.description: The key of a line and its colon; nothing for the root.

members.name: renderValue
members.description: What follows the key: a leaf's value or a branch's size summary.

members.name: highlight
members.description: Wraps each case-insensitive occurrence of the search text in a `<mark>`.

members.name: copyValue
members.description: What "copy value" puts on the clipboard for a line.

members.name: segmentsOf
members.description: The path a line reports (copied, in `expansion-change`, in `searchMatches`), from its pointer.

declarations.description:
A JSON Schema, or an OpenAPI schema object, as a tree of its properties: the documentation view of an API reference.
Each line is a property with its type (`string <email>`, `integer | null`, `Tag[]`, or the name of the schema it
refers to), its marks (`required`, `deprecated`, `read-only`, `write-only`), its constraints (`≥ 0`, `≤ 40 chars`,
`/^[A-Z]{3}$/`, `default 10`), its allowed values and its description. An object property opens on its properties,
an array of objects on its items' properties, and a `oneOf` or `anyOf` on one line per option.

```html
<c2-schema-tree schema='{"type":"object","required":["id"],"properties":{"id":{"type":"string","format":"uuid"}}}'></c2-schema-tree>
```

Local `$ref`s (`#/$defs/Address`, `#/components/schemas/Address`) are followed, `allOf` is merged, and a schema that
refers back to one of its ancestors is marked `recursive` instead of opening forever. To show one schema of an OpenAPI
document with its references, give the whole document and its pointer: `pointer="/components/schemas/Order"`.

It is `c2-json-viewer` reading a schema: the keyboard, `search` and `filter`, `expand-depth`, `expandAll()`, the
events and the `--c2-json-viewer-*` variables all work the same; `search` matches the names and the types a line
shows. Paths (copied, in `expansion-change`, in `searchMatches`) are keyword locations: the walk from the root schema,
`$ref`s included (`$.properties.address.$ref.properties.city`, or `/properties/address/$ref/properties/city` with
`path-format="pointer"`), so two properties sharing a schema still have paths of their own. "Copy value" copies the
line's schema. `data` is not used. The code that reads a schema loads the first time one is given; until then, and on
the server, the tree is empty, and if it cannot load the `empty` slot shows. A document whose expansion passes 20,000
lines stops opening beyond them.
